reference.title: Publishing output comparison
reference.shortdesc: DITA can be published in the following formats and each format has its specific use

section.p: DITA can be published in the following formats and each format has its specific use case:

row.entry: Online user assistance, responsive web help, and product documentation intended for modern browsers and mobile devices; supports dynamic layouts and JavaScriptbased search/navigation.
Webbased documentation when strict XMLcompliant HTML is required; useful for integration into XMLcentric publishing workflows and CMS environments.
Printready or downloadable manuals, release notes, and technical reports; ideal for offline distribution and regulatory or archival purposes.
Content for collaboration with subjectmatter experts in Microsoft Word; useful for review, editing, or when Word is the corporate standard.
Lightweight documentation for wikis, READMEs, or staticsite generators; good for developeroriented content and Gitbased workflows.
Ebooks and longform digital publications for ereaders and tablets; suited for training material, user guides, and content libraries.
Windowsdesktop help systems; provides a compact, indexed, searchable help file integrated with Windows applications.
Embedded help tightly linked to UI elements (for example, via F1style help); supports applicationspecific help from the same DITA source.
Browserbased help portals with search, navigation, and TOC; used for product suites, knowledge bases, and multiproject documentation centers.
Structured, topicoriented answers for conversational AI and support bots; DITA topics map to intents and responses in a chatbot.
